content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

F-Droid, the free and open-source software repository for Android, released version 2.0 on September 24, describing it as ["the largest app update in 10 years"](https://f-droid.org/2026/09/24/f-droid-2.0-a-new-chapter-for-android-freedom.html) and a complete redesign of the official client app. According to [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/F-Droid-2-0-Alternative-app-store-for-Android-gets-major-update-11465612.html), the release is "the biggest app update in ten years," ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (804 words, within the 400-1200 range). Clear section headers (Overview, What's New, Installation and Platform Changes, The Developer Verification Backdrop, What We Don't Know). Neutral, factual tone throughout with no editorializing or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources read in full from the gzipped snapshots on disk (not re-fetched). (1) sources/2026-09/f-droid-ships-version-20-its-biggest-update-in-a-decade-as-googles-developer-verification-deadline-looms/source-0.html.gz — f-droid.org's official 'F-Droid 2.0: A New Chapter for Android Freedom' blog post (Sep 24, 2026). Verified verbatim: 'largest app update in 10 years'; 'more than a year' of development and '14 test releases'; navigation simplified to 'Discover, Search and My Apps' with Settings/Nearby Swap moved to the top bar; Discover screen surfaces newly added/recently updated/most-downloaded apps; '17 different game genres' plus new VPN/password-manager/firewall categories; CJK search improvements and recent-query memory; combinable filters (category, device compatibility, anti-features); the direct quote 'thanks largely to pressure from the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) and anti-trust actions around the world' verbatim; unified installer using the new pre-approval API, confirming installs before download completes rather than after; automatic background update checks now default, pull-to-refresh repurposed to scrolling-only with manual refresh moved to the My Apps overflow menu; Tor auto-detection removed and migrated to generic Proxy Settings; the 'disguise' feature redesigned so the app remains visible in Android's app list and detectable on forensic inspection; the app-wipe-on-panic-trigger feature explicitly 'has not yet returned' with F-Droid suggesting affected users postpone updating; Android 6 support dropped (a fix landed in Android 7) and F-Droid Privileged Extension no longer used, relying on Android's native session installer; funding credits to Torsten Grote/NLnet Mobifree, OTF UX & Discovery Lab, Calyx Institute, NGI, and the OTF Security Lab/Convocation security review — all confirmed verbatim. suspicious_patterns was null; no injection content found. (2) sources/.../source-1.html.gz — heise.de (heise online), 'F-Droid 2.0: Alternative app store for Android gets major update' (Andreas Floemer). Verified verbatim: the direct quote 'the biggest app update in ten years'; Kotlin/Jetpack Compose rewrite; the same three-area navigation redesign; 17 game genres plus VPN/password-manager/firewall categories (independent confirmation of the F-Droid post's claim); unified installer + pre-approval API description, including the direct quote 'This brings the F-Droid installation experience on official Android devices much closer to what the integrated app store offers'; the verbatim quoted F-Droid blog line 'The developer registration regulation will end the F-Droid project and other free/open-source app distribution channels as we know them today'; Google's concessions (one-time setup for unverified-developer installs; free hobby accounts up to 20 devices without ID verification); and the verbatim detail 'The verification will initially take effect on September 30 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.' suspicious_patterns was null; no injection content found. No claim in the article was found unsupported by either snapshot, and both direct quotations in the article body are exact matches to the source text.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked (navigation labels, category counts, dropped/changed features, API name, funding organizations, verification rollout date and country list) traces exactly to one or both snapshots. No hallucinated or fabricated specifics found. The article correctly scopes the panic-feature claim: only the app-wipe sub-feature is described as not yet returned, while the broader 'panic' disguise feature (redesigned, not removed) is described accurately and separately — this nuance matches the source precisely rather than overstating what was dropped.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Attribution is consistently clear ('according to heise online', 'as heise online reports', 'per the same report'), and the article does not adopt F-Droid's own framing of the verification rules as existential without attributing that framing to F-Droid/heise.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article on F-Droid was found (grep across src/content/articles/ for 'f-droid' returned no hits). This is a new topic, not a duplicate or rewrite of existing coverage.
editor_notes.allowlist_action: f-droid.org was not on config/source_allowlist.txt at submission time (the sole automated finding, severity warning). F-Droid is a long-established (since 2010) free/open-source Android app repository, and the cited URL is its own official blog — a first-party primary source for its own release announcement, directly analogous to existing allowlist entries for other open-source projects' own sites (debian.org, kernel.org, openbsd.org, elixir-lang.org, tornadovm.org, four.htmx.org, etc.), each added with a comment explaining the first-party rationale. Added f-droid.org to config/source_allowlist.txt under the 'OPEN SOURCE PROJECTS' section with the same comment convention, following this precedent. Since the domain is now allowlisted and its content has been independently verified verbatim in this review, the verdict field was changed from the script's initial APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE — the underlying issue was a config gap, not a factual or attribution error in the article, so no corrections record is warranted.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced, accurately attributed submission. Both sources read in full and every specific and direct quote verified verbatim. The only automated flag (f-droid.org missing from the allowlist) was resolved by adding the domain following documented precedent for open-source projects' own sites. Approved without corrections.
